scenario_stem:
Wickmere Fruit Juices is a private limited company in Country X, owned by Carla Jimenez for 5 years. It presses apple and berry juices and sells 32,000 bottles a month to supermarkets at $2.40 each, generating $920,000 in annual revenue. The company holds a 4% share of the regional juice market, well behind market leader Purevale on 21%, and sales grew by 9% last year.

Carla must set the aims of next year's promotion with a budget of $35,000. Her marketing manager has proposed either an informative campaign explaining the new low-sugar recipe to existing customers, costed at $16,000, or a persuasive campaign using lifestyle posters and television advertising aimed at rival brand switchers, costed at $27,000. The campaign must also improve customer loyalty and support the launch of a new 750ml family-size bottle planned for the spring.

questions.question_text: Define 'promotion'.
questions.model_answer: Promotion is communicating with customers to inform, persuade or remind them about a product in order to encourage sales [2].

knowledge_max_2: communicating with customers/informing or persuading them
to encourage sales or remind them of the product

questions.question_text: Explain two aims Wickmere Fruit Juices could have for its promotion.
questions.model_answer: Aim 1: To inform existing customers about the new low-sugar recipe [k], giving clear details of what has changed in the juices they already buy [app]. Aim 2: To persuade rival brand switchers to buy Wickmere juices instead [k], helping the company grow from its 4% market share against Purevale's 21% [app].

knowledge_max_2: to inform customers/explain the product or its changes
to persuade customers to buy or switch brands

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Wickmere Fruit Juices of setting clear aims for its promotion.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Clear aims allow Carla to choose between the informative and persuasive proposals [k], so the $35,000 budget goes to the option that fits the business best [app], reducing wasted spending on the wrong method [an]. Benefit 2: Clear aims provide measurable targets, such as continued growth in bottles sold [k], letting Carla check whether sales stay ahead of the recent 9% rise [app], which helps judge whether the campaign succeeded [an].

knowledge_max_2: aims focus budget on a suitable promotional method
aims provide measurable targets to evaluate success
analysis_max_2: reduces wasted expenditure on an unsuitable method
enables the business to judge campaign success afterwards

questions.question_text: Do you think Wickmere Fruit Juices should choose the informative campaign or the persuasive campaign? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The informative campaign explains the new low-sugar recipe to existing customers [k], targeting the buyers of the 32,000 bottles sold each month [app], which should protect repeat sales and the recent 9% growth [an]. However, the persuasive campaign uses lifestyle posters and television advertising to reach rival brand switchers [k], going beyond Wickmere's 4% share against Purevale's 21% [app], which could accelerate growth of the family-size bottle if it succeeds [an]. Overall, the informative campaign is the safer choice because Carla's first priority should be keeping existing customers as the recipe changes [eval], and with a budget of $35,000 the cheaper $16,000 option leaves headroom to support the 750ml family-size bottle launch [eval].

knowledge_max_2: informative campaign: informs existing customers, lower risk
persuasive campaign: wider reach, can attract new customers
analysis_max_2: protects repeat sales and recent 9% growth
could accelerate family-size bottle success via switchers
evaluation_max_2: weighs lower-risk retention against higher-risk persuasion
justified choice given the $35,000 budget constraint

scenario_stem:
Aldermont Cycles is a private limited company in Country X founded 6 years ago by Ravi Menon. It designs and sells electric bicycles at $1,850 each from a single showroom, with annual revenue of $1.9 million and 1,020 e-bikes sold last year. The company employs 14 staff and spends $90,000 a year on marketing.

Aldermont is launching a new commuter e-bike and must choose between two advertising campaigns costing $32,000 each. One uses informative advertisements in technology magazines explaining the 90km battery range, the 2-year warranty and the crash-tested frame. The other uses persuasive advertisements on television and billboards, showing aspirational lifestyles and emphasising freedom and prestige. The board wants the launch to reach early buyers before the winter cycling season begins.

questions.question_text: Define 'informative advertising'.
questions.model_answer: Advertising that provides factual information about a product, such as its features or price, to help customers make an informed decision [2].

knowledge_max_2: advertising that gives factual information
helps customers make informed decisions

questions.question_text: Explain two differences between informative and persuasive advertising.
questions.model_answer: Difference 1: Informative advertising gives factual information about a product [k], such as the 90km battery range, the 2-year warranty and the crash-tested frame [app]. Difference 2: Persuasive advertising aims to convince customers by appealing to emotions and desires [k], using television and billboards showing freedom and prestige [app].

knowledge_max_2: informative advertising gives factual information
persuasive advertising appeals to emotions to convince

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Aldermont Cycles of using persuasive advertising for the new commuter e-bike.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Persuasive advertisements can build a desirable brand image [k], presenting the commuter e-bike as a symbol of freedom and prestige [app], which differentiates it from ordinary bicycles and encourages buyers to pay $1,850 [an]. Advantage 2: Television and billboard advertising reaches a mass audience [k], creating awareness of the new commuter e-bike beyond the single showroom [app], which should increase enquiries and showroom footfall before winter [an].

knowledge_max_2: builds brand image/desire for the product
reaches large audiences quickly
analysis_max_2: differentiates the product and supports premium pricing
raises enquiries and footfall ahead of launch

questions.question_text: Do you think Aldermont Cycles should use informative advertising or persuasive advertising for the new e-bike launch? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The informative campaign suits a high-price product like the $1,850 e-bike, because readers of technology magazines want hard facts such as the 90km range and 2-year warranty [k], giving technically minded buyers the confidence to visit the single showroom and test-ride [app], which lowers the risk of wasted visits [an]. However, the persuasive campaign on television and billboards reaches a much wider audience [k], embedding the e-bike as a symbol of freedom and prestige [app], which could pull in aspirational buyers who would never read technology magazines [an]. Overall, Aldermont should choose informative advertising because the $32,000 must justify a considered, high-involvement purchase rather than impulse desire [eval], and prestige imagery alone rarely convinces someone spending $1,850 without technical proof [eval].

knowledge_max_2: informative ads: supports high-involvement decisions
persuasive ads: wider emotional reach/aspiration
analysis_max_2: reduces risk of unsuitable buyers visiting showroom
broadens reach beyond technical readers
evaluation_max_2: weighs considered purchase against mass emotional reach
justified preference for technical proof at this price point

scenario_stem:
Bramfield Supermarket is a private limited company in Country X with 6 branches and 480 staff. It generated $14.6 million in revenue last year, and breakfast cereals account for 11% of all sales. Annual marketing expenditure is $210,000, of which $60,000 has been allocated to cereal promotions over the next quarter. Rival discounters have been cutting staple prices aggressively across the region, winning back families on tight budgets.

The marketing manager wants to increase cereal sales by 20% in the next quarter. Two options are available: a buy-one-get-one-free (BOGOF) offer across 14 cereal brands, or a straight 15% price reduction on the same 14 brands. Suppliers have agreed to fund half of the cost of whichever promotion is chosen this quarter.

questions.question_text: Define 'sales promotion'.
questions.model_answer: Short-term incentives used to encourage customers to buy a product or to boost sales of it, such as discounts or special offers [2].

knowledge_max_2: short-term incentives to buy
used to boost sales of a product

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Bramfield Supermarket of using a BOGOF offer on cereal.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: BOGOF can rapidly increase sales volume [k], helping the supermarket reach its target of a 20% rise in cereal sales across the 6 branches [app]. Advantage 2: BOGOF attracts customers into the supermarket [k], where they may buy other products alongside the 14 cereal brands [app].

knowledge_max_2: rapidly increases sales volume
attracts customers into the store (footfall)

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Bramfield Supermarket of the suppliers funding half the promotion.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: Funding halves the supermarket's net cost of the promotion [k], so the $60,000 allocation stretches further whichever option is chosen [app], keeping money available within the wider $210,000 marketing budget [an]. Benefit 2: Suppliers fund the activity because higher sales also benefit their own brands [k], so they share the risk on the 14 cereal brands [app], which strengthens the long-term trading relationship [an].

knowledge_max_2: reduces supermarket's net promotional cost
shared risk with suppliers seeking higher sales
analysis_max_2: keeps budget available for other marketing
strengthens supplier relationships and cooperation

valid_app_words: Suppliers have agreed to fund half

questions.question_text: Do you think Bramfield Supermarket should use the BOGOF offer or the 15% price reduction on its cereal brands? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The BOGOF offer creates a strong short-term incentive, because shoppers pay full price for one box and receive a second box free [k], which could push cereal sales up sharply towards the 20% target across all 14 brands [app], clearing stock quickly and drawing in price-conscious families [an]. However, the 15% price reduction is simpler for staff and customers to understand [k], lowering the shelf price of every box without giving away extra units [app], protecting margins if BOGOF would halve the value of each sale at higher volume [an]. Overall, Bramfield should choose BOGOF because the suppliers fund half the cost either way, making the free extra units affordable [eval], and a dramatic offer is more likely to achieve a 20% quarterly uplift than a modest 15% discount during rival price cuts [eval].

knowledge_max_2: BOGOF: strong instant incentive, drives volume
price reduction: simple, protects unit margins/understanding
application_max_2: suppliers funding half of either option
analysis_max_2: clears stock quickly, attracts price-sensitive shoppers
simpler administration and preserves margins per unit
evaluation_max_2: weighs dramatic volume-driving offer against simpler discount
justified choice given shared funding and rival price pressure

scenario_stem:
Thistlebrook Snacks is a private limited company in Country X, owned by Devon Okafor for 3 years. It produces baked lentil and chickpea snacks sold at $1.60 per 150g bag through 900 convenience stores, generating $780,000 in annual revenue. A new chilli-lime flavour is due to launch in May, and its target market is health-conscious commuters who eat on the way to work.

To promote the new flavour, the sales manager is choosing between two options. The first is distributing 10,000 free 50g sample bags at railway stations and gyms, costing $14,000. The second is running a competition where shoppers enter the code inside packs to win a $5,000 holiday voucher, costing $17,000 in prizes and administration over three months.

questions.question_text: Define 'free samples'.
questions.model_answer: Free trial-size giveaways of a product offered to customers so they can taste or test it before buying [2].

knowledge_max_2: free trial-size giveaways/samples of a product
allow customers to test before buying

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Thistlebrook Snacks of distributing 10,000 free sample bags.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Free samples let potential customers try the new chilli-lime flavour before buying [k], encouraging first-time trial among health-conscious commuters [app]. Advantage 2: Samples handed out at railway stations and gyms reach the target market directly [k], where 900 convenience stores can turn fresh awareness into repeat purchases [app].

knowledge_max_2: lets customers try before buying (trial)
targeted distribution reaches the intended market

questions.question_text: Explain two problems Thistlebrook Snacks could face when running the competition.
questions.model_answer: Problem 1: The competition costs $17,000, more than the $14,000 needed for samples [k], and the code inside packs means only people who already buy the snacks can enter [app], so it may not attract new customers at all [an]. Problem 2: Competition entries depend entirely on customer participation [k], and a hidden or unclear code could mean very few entries [app], wasting the $5,000 prize money and three months of administration [an].

knowledge_max_2: higher cost than alternatives/aims at existing buyers only
success depends on customer participation and clarity of entry method
analysis_max_2: may fail to attract new customers
wasted prize spend and effort if participation is low

questions.question_text: Do you think Thistlebrook Snacks should use free samples or the in-pack competition to promote the new chilli-lime flavour? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Free samples cost $14,000 and put the new chilli-lime flavour directly into the hands of health-conscious commuters at railway stations and gyms [k], generating word-of-mouth and immediate trial at the 900 convenience stores [app], which should drive first-time purchases and launch momentum [an]. However, the competition costs $17,000 yet reaches only buyers who already pick up a 150g bag [k], making it a tool for loyalty and repeat purchase rather than new trial [app], so it suits retention more than launch awareness [an]. Overall, Thistlebrook should choose free samples because the central challenge is getting the new flavour tried, not retaining existing buyers [eval], and the lower cost frees $3,000 to support distribution across the 900 stores [eval].

knowledge_max_2: samples: drive trial among new customers
competition: rewards existing buyers, builds repeat purchases
analysis_max_2: stimulates first-time purchase and launch awareness
better suited to retention than trial
evaluation_max_2: weighs launch trial against loyalty repeat purchase
justified choice given target of launching a new flavour

scenario_stem:
Elmwick Teas is a family-run private limited company in Country X, trading for 8 years. It sells premium loose-leaf tea at $6.80 per 100g tin through 240 independent delis, generating $1.3 million in annual revenue. Independent research shows only 3 in 10 shoppers notice the Elmwick brand on deli shelves, and repeat purchase rates are below target, with many delis reporting empty shelf gaps on busy weekends.

Elmwick has $22,000 for promotion this year. The managing director must choose between a free branded tea infuser gift with every 2 tins purchased, costing $15,000, or point-of-sale displays for all 240 delis, including counter stands, shelf signage and a staff briefing pack, costing $18,000, funded jointly with the delis' cooperation this spring.

questions.question_text: Define 'point-of-sale display'.
questions.model_answer: Promotional materials placed where a purchase is made, such as shelf signage or counter stands, designed to attract shoppers' attention [2].

knowledge_max_2: promotional materials placed at the point of purchase
designed to attract shoppers' attention

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Elmwick Teas of using point-of-sale displays in delis.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Displays make the Elmwick brand more visible at the moment of purchase [k], helping more than 3 in 10 shoppers notice Elmwick on deli shelves [app]. Advantage 2: Displays for all 240 delis cost $18,000 [k], which fits within the $22,000 promotion budget [app].

knowledge_max_2: increases brand visibility at the point of purchase
affordable/high reach per unit of spend

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Elmwick Teas of offering the free branded tea infuser gift.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: A free gift encourages customers to buy more tins per visit [k], increasing the number of $6.80 tins sold at each deli [app], which raises the average spend per transaction [an]. Benefit 2: A branded infuser keeps the Elmwick name visible in customers' homes [k], reinforcing loyalty every time tea is brewed [app], which should defend the $1.3 million annual revenue [an].

knowledge_max_2: gift increases units purchased per visit
gift keeps brand visible at home, builds loyalty
analysis_max_2: raises average transaction value
protects revenue through repeat loyalty

questions.question_text: Do you think Elmwick Teas should choose the free branded tea infuser gift or the point-of-sale displays? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The point-of-sale displays attack the core problem identified by research: only 3 in 10 shoppers notice Elmwick on deli shelves [k], and better visibility across 240 stores should convert passing shoppers into buyers at $6.80 per tin [app], directly lifting sales volume and against the below-target repeat rate [an]. However, the free tea infuser gift with every 2 tins turns loyal shoppers into visible brand ambassadors at home [k], rewarding repeat purchase and keeping Elmwick in the kitchen cupboard [app], which deepens relationships that shelf signage cannot [an]. Overall, Elmwick should choose point-of-sale displays because awareness is the bottleneck the research exposes [eval], and at $18,000 it fits the $22,000 budget while leaving $4,000 for deli cooperation and restocking support [eval].

knowledge_max_2: displays: increase visibility at moment of purchase
gift: rewards loyalty, increases purchase frequency
application_max_2: only 3 in 10 shoppers notice the brand
analysis_max_2: converts shoppers into buyers at shelf
builds deeper home-based brand loyalty
evaluation_max_2: weighs shelf visibility against in-home loyalty
justified choice given research bottleneck and budget fit

scenario_stem:
Kestrelmere Machine Tools is a private limited company in Country X, founded 11 years ago by Petra Volkov. It manufactures and services industrial metal presses at $85,000 each, selling around 24 units a year to factories and generating $2.05 million from press sales per year. It employs 26 engineers and 3 sales representatives, each covering a different industrial region of the country, with servicing contracts worth a further $400,000 per year.

Kestrelmere must increase press sales by 4 units next year to justify a planned factory extension. The finance director favours hiring 2 additional sales representatives on 3% commission of each sale. The marketing director instead wants to exhibit at the National Manufacturing Show, costing $38,000 for the stand, travel and demonstration rigs across three days.

questions.question_text: Define 'personal selling'.
questions.model_answer: Direct, face-to-face communication between a salesperson and a customer with the aim of persuading that customer to buy a product [2].

knowledge_max_2: direct/face-to-face communication
to persuade a customer to buy

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Kestrelmere Machine Tools of using personal selling.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Personal selling lets representatives explain the technical features of an $85,000 press in detail [k], answering factory buyers' questions directly [app]. Advantage 2: Representatives can build long-term relationships with industrial customers [k], supporting repeat press sales and servicing contracts [app].

knowledge_max_2: can explain technical features/handle complex products
builds long-term customer relationships

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Kestrelmere Machine Tools of exhibiting at the National Manufacturing Show.
questions.model_answer: Benefit 1: A trade show stand exposes Kestrelmere to many factory buyers in one place [k], reaching more qualified prospects in three days than 2 extra representatives could visit in months [app], generating a faster flow of sales leads [an]. Benefit 2: Live demonstrations of the demonstration rigs attract serious buyers [k], letting buyers see the industrial metal presses in action before committing to $85,000 [app], which can shorten the decision-making process [an].

knowledge_max_2: reaches many prospects in one concentrated venue
demonstrations build buyer confidence for high-value purchases
analysis_max_2: generates sales leads faster than territory visits
shortens long purchase decision cycles

questions.question_text: Do you think Kestrelmere Machine Tools should hire 2 additional sales representatives or exhibit at the National Manufacturing Show? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Hiring 2 representatives on 3% commission means pay rises only when sales rise [k], protecting cash while directly targeting the 4 extra presses needed for the factory extension [app], and strengthening territory coverage for deepening relationships with factories [an]. However, the National Manufacturing Show costs $38,000 up front but concentrates dozens of serious factory buyers in one exhibition hall [k], letting Petra's team show the demonstration rigs, gather competitor intelligence and win orders that territory calls rarely secure quickly [app], which could deliver the 4 units in weeks rather than months [an]. Overall, Kestrelmere should exhibit at the show because the planned factory extension depends on landing a few large contracts quickly [eval], and the show offers a concentrated, time-bound route to qualified buyers that commission-based hiring cannot guarantee [eval].

knowledge_max_2: commission-only reps align pay with sales results
exhibition concentrates many qualified buyers in one place
application_max_2: 4 extra presses for the factory extension
analysis_max_2: protects cash flow but adds ongoing labour cost
show can compress a long sales cycle into days
evaluation_max_2: weighs steady territory coverage against concentrated exposure
justified choice given urgency of factory extension target

scenario_stem:
Breakwater Energy Drinks is a private limited company in Country X, set up 4 years ago by sisters Daniela and Sofia Herrera. It produces sugar-free energy drinks at $1.20 per 330ml can, stocked in 6,500 retailers, generating $3.4 million in annual revenue. The brand is popular with 16 to 30 year olds but awareness outside this group is low, and sales grew just 2% last year.

Breakwater must decide how to spend a $75,000 promotional budget. One option is a two-year sponsorship of Portmere Athletic FC at $30,000 per season, including pitch-side advertising seen by 12,000 fans per home game. The other is a public relations campaign: sponsoring a national beach clean-up with 5,000 volunteers and issuing press releases to lifestyle magazines and television.

questions.question_text: Define 'sponsorship'.
questions.model_answer: Supporting an event, person or organisation financially or with resources in return for brand exposure and association [2].

knowledge_max_2: financially supporting an event/person/organisation
in return for brand exposure/association

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Breakwater Energy Drinks of sponsoring Portmere Athletic FC.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Pitch-side advertising reaches 12,000 fans per home game [k], repeatedly exposing the brand to the 16 to 30 year olds who already buy the drinks [app]. Advantage 2: Sponsorship associates the brand with sport, energy and excitement [k], reinforcing the positioning of the sugar-free energy drinks at $1.20 per can [app].

knowledge_max_2: repeated brand exposure to target audience
brand association with sport/energy values

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Breakwater Energy Drinks of the public relations beach clean-up campaign.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Public relations coverage in lifestyle magazines and television can reach audiences beyond the current 16 to 30 year old base [k], widening awareness of the $1.20 can among older and non-fan drinkers [app], helping the brand grow beyond its existing segment [an]. Advantage 2: Supporting a beach clean-up with 5,000 volunteers builds a positive, responsible image [k], earning goodwill that paid advertising cannot buy [app], which should strengthen trust and reputation in the Breakwater brand [an].

knowledge_max_2: PR can reach audiences beyond current target segments
PR builds positive image/goodwill at lower cost
analysis_max_2: expands awareness beyond core young segment
strengthens trust and reputation

questions.question_text: Do you think Breakwater Energy Drinks should sponsor Portmere Athletic FC or run the public relations beach clean-up campaign? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The FC sponsorship costs $30,000 per season and guarantees pitch-side exposure to 12,000 fans per home game [k], repeatedly reaching the 16 to 30 year olds who already buy the sugar-free cans [app], reinforcing loyalty and purchase frequency among a proven audience [an]. However, the public relations campaign with 5,000 volunteers and national magazine coverage [k] can lift awareness far beyond the current segment and cost less per person reached than $60,000 over two seasons [app], positioning Breakwater as environmentally responsible at a time when growth has slowed to 2% [an]. Overall, Breakwater should choose the sponsorship because its proven young sports audience matches the core 16 to 30 year old market [eval], giving clearer and more measurable returns than an uncertain public relations campaign [eval].

knowledge_max_2: sponsorship: guaranteed repeated exposure to a known audience
PR: wider reach, favourable image, lower measurability
analysis_max_2: reinforces loyalty and purchase frequency in core market
broadens awareness and improves image when growth is slow
evaluation_max_2: weighs targeted, measurable exposure against broader but riskier reach
justified choice given core audience match

scenario_stem:
Harbour & Lark Streetwear is an online clothing business in Country X, founded 2 years ago by Zoe Banks. It sells graphic hoodies at $45 and caps at $22, generating $520,000 in annual revenue, with 85% of sales through its website and social pages and 38,000 followers. It has no full-time marketing staff, and growth has slowed from 60% in year one to 12% last year.

Zoe wants to attract customers aged 13 to 24. She is deciding between a $9,000 paid social media campaign of targeted advertisements over 3 months, and a $2,500 viral stunt: a limited run of 500 artist-designed hoodies seeded to 2 micro-influencers, hoping the drop video is shared widely online within the first fortnight of release.

questions.question_text: Define 'viral marketing'.
questions.model_answer: A promotional approach that encourages people to share a message about a product or brand so it spreads rapidly and widely online [2].

knowledge_max_2: message designed to be shared by users themselves
spreads rapidly and widely online

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to Harbour & Lark Streetwear of using social media to promote its products.
questions.model_answer: Advantage 1: Social media advertising can target specific age groups [k], focusing the $9,000 campaign on customers aged 13 to 24 [app]. Advantage 2: Social pages already drive 85% of Harbour & Lark's sales [k], so promotion sits on the channels where its customers are already buying [app].

knowledge_max_2: can target specific audience demographics
promotes on channels already used by customers

questions.question_text: Explain two problems Harbour & Lark Streetwear could face from the viral stunt.
questions.model_answer: Problem 1: Success in viral marketing is unpredictable [k], and the 500 artist-designed hoodies might sell out without ever trending online [app], wasting the $2,500 and the micro-influencers' effort [an]. Problem 2: Negative publicity spreads as fast as positive publicity [k], so a criticised video could damage the reputation built by 38,000 followers [app], weakening trust among existing customers [an].

knowledge_max_2: unpredictable/uncontrollable whether content goes viral
negative publicity risk spreads fast online
analysis_max_2: wasted spend if the video never trends
reputation damage weakens existing customer trust

questions.question_text: Do you think Harbour & Lark Streetwear should choose the $9,000 paid social media campaign or the $2,500 viral stunt? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The paid campaign spends $9,000 on 3 months of targeted advertisements aimed at 13 to 24 year olds [k], delivering predictable, measurable reach into the website and social pages behind 85% of revenue [app], making sales impact easier to forecast and optimise [an]. However, the viral stunt costs only $2,500 and could reach far more people if the drop video is shared widely [k], creating buzz around the limited 500-unit run that no fixed advertising budget could buy [app], punching far above its weight for a bootstrapped brand with no marketing staff [an]. Overall, Zoe should choose the paid campaign because reliable, targeted reach matters more than lottery-odds virality [eval], and her limited budget cannot comfortably absorb $2,500 on a stunt that may never trend [eval].

knowledge_max_2: paid social ads: predictable, measurable targeting
viral stunt: potentially huge reach, low certainty
analysis_max_2: forecastable, optimisable return on ad spend
cheap high-impact buzz if video is shared widely
evaluation_max_2: weighs reliable targeting against low-odds high-reward virality
justified choice given limited budget and no marketing staff

scenario_stem:
Bramble & Ink Books is an independent bookshop in Country X, opened 7 years ago by Hugo Lindgren in a market town of 28,000 people. It employs 5 staff, sells books at an average price of $14, and generated $390,000 in revenue last year. National chains and online retailers undercut its prices by 10 to 20%, and footfall has fallen 15% in the past two years, with weekday evenings noticeably quieter than before.

Hugo wants to modernise the marketing mix. He is deciding between $26,000 on a new e-commerce website with an email newsletter and targeted online advertising, or $13,000 on an in-store experience upgrade: author evenings, a coffee corner and point-of-sale displays, supported by local radio advertising across the town.

questions.question_text: Define 'e-commerce'.
questions.model_answer: Buying and selling goods or services over the internet, such as through a website or online marketplace [2].

knowledge_max_2: buying and selling goods/services over the internet

questions.question_text: Explain two opportunities e-commerce offers Bramble & Ink Books.
questions.model_answer: Opportunity 1: An e-commerce website lets the shop sell to customers beyond the market town of 28,000 people [k], reaching readers across the country [app]. Opportunity 2: Online ordering is open all day every day [k], letting customers buy at the average price of $14 at any time [app].

questions.question_text: Explain two problems Bramble & Ink Books could face selling through a new e-commerce website.
questions.model_answer: Problem 1: E-commerce pits Bramble & Ink against national chains and online retailers undercutting prices by 10 to 20% [k], so matching them online could squeeze thin margins [app], threatening profitability despite extra volume [an]. Problem 2: Building and running the website costs $26,000 up front [k], a heavy burden on a shop generating $390,000 in annual revenue [app], making returns depend on sustained online orders [an].

knowledge_max_2: faces intense online price competition
significant up-front and ongoing cost of the channel
analysis_max_2: margin erosion from price matching
slow payback on the investment

questions.question_text: Do you think Hugo should spend $26,000 on the e-commerce website or $13,000 on the in-store experience upgrade? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The e-commerce website costs $26,000 but removes the geographical ceiling of a town of 28,000 people [k], letting the shop sell at an average price of $14 to online customers everywhere and collect emails via the newsletter [app], creating a scalable new revenue stream [an]. However, the in-store upgrade costs only $13,000 and plays to the local shop's strengths [k], using author evenings and a coffee corner to build a community that online chains cannot copy [app], deepening local loyalty and weekday footfall [an]. Overall, Hugo should choose the in-store upgrade because differentiation through experience is cheaper to defend than a national price war online [eval], and it risks $13,000 rather than $26,000 of a modest $390,000 revenue base [eval].

knowledge_max_2: e-commerce: expands reach but high cost and price competition
experience upgrade: deepens local differentiation and loyalty
analysis_max_2: scalable new online revenue stream
defendable local community advantage
evaluation_max_2: weighs scalable reach against cheaper defensible local loyalty
justified choice given modest revenue and budget risk

scenario_stem:
Embergate Cinema is a 4-screen cinema in Country X, owned by Marcus Whitfield since 2019. It sells 95,000 tickets a year at $11 each, earning $1.045 million in ticket revenue, plus $260,000 from food and drink. Monday to Thursday attendance has fallen by 28% over the past year, leaving weekday screenings half-empty, while weekend sessions sell out and customer satisfaction remains high among regulars.

To reverse the decline, the manager is choosing between two January promotions.
